note: Loan-product CONFIGURATION read-back (GET /loanproducts, /loanproducts/template, /loanproducts/{id}). The loanproduct package owns the stored-value <-> enum tables (amortization/interest/interest-calc-period/frequency/day-count) and the LoanProductRelatedDetail value object; the schedule/EMI arithmetic that consumes those values is already owned and graded by loanschedule under DEC-1, so this context grades the CONFIGURATION, not the money the schedule projects from it. The one non-obvious discriminator is the day-count trap: DaysInYearType and DaysInMonthType store the literal day count, not the ordinal (DaysInYear360=360, DaysInYear364=364, DaysInYear365=365, DaysInMonth30=30), so a naive iota port is silently wrong on every non-trivial day-count convention.

roundingSurface.seam: none — the loan-product CONFIGURATION carries values verbatim
roundingSurface.note: principal, interestRatePerPeriod and annualInterestRate are carried numeric(19,6) columns with NO decode or rounding in the loanproduct package (the annual-nominal-rate derivation is deferred to loanschedule under DEC-1). No HALF_UP/HALF_EVEN tie exists on this surface. The discriminator this context pins is not a rounding tie but the stored-value != ordinal day-count trap (DaysInYear360 stores 360, DaysInMonth30 stores 30).

vocabularySources.periodFrequency: loanproducts-template-raw.json repaymentFrequencyTypeOptions / interestRateFrequencyTypeOptions; the DTO prepends 'repaymentFrequency.' / 'interestRateFrequency.' to the enum's own getCode() (PeriodFrequencyType.java:26-31)
vocabularySources.daysInMonth: loanproducts-template-raw.json daysInMonthTypeOptions (id 1 actual, id 30 days360 — stored value is the literal day count, NOT the ordinal)
vocabularySources.daysInYear: loanproducts-template-raw.json daysInYearTypeOptions (id 1 actual, id 360 days360, id 364 days364, id 365 days365 — stored value is the literal day count, NOT the ordinal)
